newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU said to probe Michelin sales practice.
newsitem.headline: EU said to probe Michelin sales practice.

text.p: The European Commission is probing French tyre group Michelin's sales practices in the European market, a Commission source told Reuters on Tuesday.

"The Commission is studying certain practices in the European Community tyre market. According to the information that the Commission has, inequitable commercial conditions are allegedly being imposed by a company occupying a dominant position," an EC document obtained by Reuters in Paris said.
"If the existence of these practices were confirmed, they could constitute an infringement of article 86 of the European Commission treaty," the letter dated December 30, 1996 said.
A Commission source in Brussels confirmed that Michelin was the subject of the investigation. "I can tell you that is true," the source said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The Commission has not made public any probe into Michelin and its spokesman's office did not reply to Reuter enquiries on the case.
A spokesman for Michelin, Europe's leading tyremaker, told Reuters: "There is no comment on our part."
The Commission letter was accompanied by a questionnaire apparently directed at tyre distributors, seeking information on Michelin's rebate system. It requested responses by February 10.

It said the request was based on an EU regulation, "which enables the Commission to gather all information necessary from enterprises and associations of enterprises, whether or not they are suspected of having infringed the rules of competition".

In a section titled "Michelin's Commercial Policy", the questionnaire asked: "Provide copies of your supply contracts for Michelin tyre since 1985. Are these contracts based on Michelin's usual General Conditions of Sale?"

It then asked: "Do Michelin's General Conditions of Sale establish three categories of rebates (quantity rebates, service quality and rebates determined as a function of efforts to sell new tyres?) How are these rebates calculated? When are they paid? For how long has this system existed?"
It also asked whether other tyre makers employed similar rebate systems.
The Commission source said the case was not related to a proposed joint venture between Compagnie Financiere Michelin and Continental AG of Germany.
The EC said in August it proposed to clear the venture and was seeking comment from interested parties before announcing a final decision.
The source declined to say whether the Michelin probe had been prompted by a complaint, or whether any other tyre manufacturers were under investigation.
